newsitem.title: UK: United Gas wins 4 mln stg appeal against NatPower.
newsitem.headline: United Gas wins 4 mln stg appeal against NatPower.

text.p: British gas marketer United Gas said on Tuesday that it had won a court appeal against power firm and gas producer National Power in a dispute over a gas supply contract.
United Gas, a wholly-owned subsidiary of United States energy company UtiliCorp United Inc., argued that deliveries of gas had not been made in accordance with the supply agreement.
It also said that National Power's refusal to explain its delivery statement, upon which payments were demanded, had been a breach of contract.
"The explanations given by National Power of the relevant "December' deliveries have changed frequently and have often been self-contradictory," said Lord Justice Hobhouse in his judgement.
The contract for the supply of 40-million cubic feet a day of North Sea gas delivered to the U.K.'s Bacton terminal started in October 1993.
United unilaterally terminated the contract in May 1995.
The court ordered National Power to repay United Gas approximately 4 million stg and pay half of the latter's costs.
United Gas was also granted unconditional leave to defend the case at a full trial.
"We are confident that at full trial all the aspects of this affair will be brought into the open," said a United Gas spokesman in a statement.
